facts.raw_span: 1 hour of acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to his left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea
similar chest pain at rest that resolved spontaneously after 30 minutes
hypertension for 5 years, treated with reserpine
Initial serum troponin I level: 1.159 ng/mL
95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery
1 hour of acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to his left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea
similar chest pain at rest that resolved spontaneously after 30 minutes
hypertension for 5 years, treated with reserpine

95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery

concepts.why: The patient presented with acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to his left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea, which is consistent with ACS.
The patient had elevated serum troponin I level and 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery, which is consistent with MI.
The patient had chest pain at rest that resolved spontaneously after 30 minutes, which is consistent with UA.
The patient had hypertension for 5 years and left ventricular ejection fraction of 57%, which is consistent with HHD.
The patient had nausea and chest pain, which can be consistent with GERD.
The patient had respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation of 96% on room air, which can be consistent with PE.
The patient had respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute, which can be consistent with pneumonia.
The patient had nausea, which can be consistent with cholecystitis.

rationales.F01: The patient's symptoms of acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to the left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea, are highly suggestive of an acute coronary syndrome.
rationales.F02: The patient's history of similar chest pain at rest that resolved spontaneously after 30 minutes is consistent with unstable angina.
rationales.F09: The elevated serum troponin I level is a strong indicator of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F10: The 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery is a strong indicator of acute coronary syndrome and myocardial infarction.
